title: Price heterogeneous native stages with all changed main and idle ranks (no new κ)
body:
Test one changed native demand outside the full/query-only stage alphabet: lower both main exit charts on the 60 actual ports whose central line lies in ker(1), retaining all 112 central jobs, the other 52 ports, 408 independent helpers, eight paid centers and shared late native-map constraints.

The bounded binary discovery returns the original native paid profile plus 120 H1 and unchanged helpers. Numerical optimality is not an exact bound. Repricing the actual p16 main and idle children rejects this returned invoice. A written derivative/incidence argument proves that every nonempty subset of these 18 returned stage invoices worsens target-minus-paid margin by at least 1038/5 per changed stage for C in [0,.0034]. This theorem concerns the returned cost, not every possible realization of the new endpoints. At the source comparison price, all single-stage margins are about -237.8; no higher κ or native admission is claimed.

Validation: registered normal/optimized standard-library replay passes. It binds all 120 changed endpoints, reconstructs the complete local and controller bill, checks exact outward moment intervals, certifies the all-subset incidence/derivative bound and rejects invalid stage/fixed-output mutations. Frozen inputs and selected κ=.00302015 remain unchanged. Signed native synthesis, changed Gaussian endpoint/normalizers, both physical orientations, compiler/precision/outer and Lean obligations remain unrun. The optimistic price screen grants those endpoint ranks and still loses.

Credit Cao Yifan/intqwq, Cinna Davis/1337isnot1337, Dugongue, Matarener, zxv, Jacob Alan Sussman and retained native/helper/compiler contributors. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. This follows the no-gain fixed-demand alphabet in #5212 and stops this returned partial-stage invoice rather than starting an output-mask census.
